text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone seeing it for the first time. One key idea is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can quickly understand their purpose. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because when you need to fix a bug or add a new feature, you can find the right place quickly. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces mistakes for everyone on the team.
